simplified.title: Om gutten som gikk til nordavinden og krevde melet tilbake

english.title: The Boy Who Went to the North Wind and Demanded His Meal Back

world: Old rural Norway at the first frost of late autumn. The boy and his mother live in a small, grey, weathered log cottage with a turf roof; beside it stands a little storehouse on posts with a steep wooden stair up to its door. Far to the north, on a bare, windswept fell where every tree leans south, stands the North Wind's house, a low, crooked log house with a sod roof weighed down with stones. On the road between them lies the inn, a big, low log house with a lantern at the door and a goat shed behind. The meal is carried in a grey sack. The magic cloth is a square white linen tablecloth with a red woven zigzag border, and the swapped one looks exactly the same. The stick is a knobbly old stick of pale birch wood, about as long as the boy is tall.
palette: Blustery late autumn at the first frost: rimed grass and bare birches, cold blue-grey skies with fast, torn clouds, and snow already lying on the northern fells where the North Wind lives. Indoors, warm firelight and glowing embers against cold blue windows. Accents: flour white, lingonberry red and pewter grey.

cast.look: A small, skinny boy of about eleven with a narrow, pale face, cheeks reddened by the cold, big sticking-out ears, bright blue eyes, a stubborn little frown and white-blond hair that sticks up in tufts. He wears a grey knitted jumper several sizes too big, patched dark-brown trousers, thick grey socks, heavy scuffed boots and a long brown knitted scarf wound twice round his neck.
cast.portrait: Background: the storehouse on posts in the frosty yard.

simplified.name: Gutten
simplified.description: En fattig, sta og modig gutt som nekter å finne seg i urett og drar ut for å kreve melet tilbake.

english.name: The Boy
english.description: A determined, practical youth who refuses to accept being robbed and is brave enough to demand justice from the North Wind.

cast.look: A thin, frail old woman of about sixty-five, a little stooped, with a long, gentle, deeply lined face, tired grey eyes, a thin mouth and one eyebrow often raised in doubt. Her grey hair hangs in one thin braid over her shoulder. She wears a faded plum-coloured homespun dress, a darned brown knitted shawl, a long patched linen apron and wooden clogs.
cast.portrait: Background: the dim cottage room by the hearth.

simplified.name: Moren
simplified.description: En gammel, fattig og skrøpelig kvinne som tviler på mirakler, men som trenger hjelpen gutten prøver å skaffe.

english.name: The Old Mother
english.description: Poor and frail, she depends on her son for food and doubts miracles until she sees them with her own eyes.

cast.look: A huge, grumbling old man made of swirling white and pale-grey cloud, with no legs, only a long, whirling tail of mist and snowflakes. He has a broad, weathered face with puffed-out round cheeks, icy-blue eyes, great bushy white eyebrows, a thick moustache like drifted snow and a long, frosty white beard that streams away in the wind, and big, soft hands of cloud. Snowflakes and tiny icicles glitter in his tangled white hair.
cast.portrait: Background: the windswept northern fells, where every tree leans south.

simplified.name: Nordavinden
simplified.description: En kraftfull og lunefull vind som først tar, men som også gir magiske gaver som erstatning.

english.name: The North Wind
english.description: A blunt, powerful force given a voice and a home, both feared and strangely fair when confronted directly.

cast.look: A tall, gangly innkeeper of about fifty with a long, narrow face, a much too wide, toothy smile, small glittering eyes, a long pointed chin and oily black hair twisted into one big curl on his forehead. He wears a wine-red waistcoat with shiny brass buttons over a white linen shirt with rolled sleeves, a long blue-and-white striped apron, dark breeches and a wide black leather money belt that jingles with coins.

simplified.name: Gjestgiveren
simplified.description: En lur krovert som stjeler de magiske gavene, men blir stoppet når gutten gjennomskuer ham.

english.name: The Innkeeper
english.description: A greedy schemer who tries to swap magical treasures for worthless lookalikes and is finally forced to return what he stole.

cast.look: A small, sturdy billy goat about the size of a large dog, with a shaggy snow-white coat, a light-grey face with a little pointed grey beard, bright amber eyes with slot-shaped pupils, short, curved, ridged horns, a stubby tail and neat black hooves. Around his neck he wears a red leather collar hung with two small brass bells.
cast.portrait: Background: the frosty yard in front of the inn.

simplified.name: Bukken
simplified.description: En magisk bukk som kan lage gullpenger når gutten sier de riktige ordene.

english.name: The Billy-Goat
english.description: A seemingly ordinary goat gifted by the North Wind, enchanted to produce gold ducats on command.

places.name: the Inn Parlour
places.look: A big, low-ceilinged parlour in an old log inn, with dark, smoke-stained timber walls, a large open fireplace, two long plank tables with benches, a small corner table under a frosted window, an iron lantern hanging from a beam, pewter mugs on a shelf and a heavy plank door to the frosty yard. Warm, smoky and golden.

cover.prompt: On a steep, windswept path high on a bare fell, the Boy leans hard into the gale with his fists clenched and his long scarf streaming out behind him, not giving an inch. Ahead of him the huge face of the North Wind fills the grey sky, cheeks puffed out and bushy eyebrows bristling, blowing a flurry of snow straight at him. The few trees on the slope all lean the same way.

simplified.caption: Gutten gikk rett til Nordavinden for å kreve melet tilbake.
simplified.alt: Gutten lener seg mot vinden på en bratt sti oppe på fjellet. Foran ham fyller Nordavinden himmelen og blåser snø rett mot ham.

english.caption: The boy went straight to the North Wind to demand his meal back.
english.alt: The boy leans into the gale on a steep mountain path. Ahead of him the North Wind fills the sky, blowing snow straight at him.

illustrations.prompt: A blustery autumn morning in a frosty farmyard beside a small grey log cottage. On the steep wooden stair of the little storehouse on posts, the Boy leans back with all his weight, clinging on as the grey sack is torn from his arms and bursts open in mid-air. The North Wind swoops down out of the torn grey clouds with his cheeks puffed out, and the meal whirls up and away across the yard in a long white cloud of dust and straw.

simplified.anchor: Men i det samme han kom ut på stabburstrappa med sekken, kom Nordavinden fykende over gårdsplassen.
simplified.caption: Nordavinden fór til værs med melet.
simplified.alt: Gutten står på stabburstrappa og holder igjen alt han orker, men sekken revner, og Nordavinden blåser melet til værs i en hvit sky av støv og halmstrå.

english.anchor: But just as he stepped out onto the storehouse steps with the sack in his arms
english.caption: The North Wind whirled the meal up into the sky.
english.alt: The boy clings to the sack on the storehouse steps, but the North Wind tears it from his arms and whirls the meal up into the sky in a white cloud.

illustrations.prompt: Far in the north on a bare, windswept fell, where every birch and pine leans south, the Boy stands in front of a low, crooked log house with a sod roof weighed down with stones. The huge North Wind leans down over the house out of the grey sky, gruff but not unkind, and holds out a neatly folded white tablecloth with a red zigzag border in one big cloudy hand. The Boy reaches up to take it, snow swirling round his boots.

simplified.anchor: «Jeg har ikke noe mel», sa Nordavinden.
simplified.caption: «Men siden du er så ille ute, skal du få en duk.»
simplified.alt: Langt mot nord, der alle trærne står på skrå, bøyer Nordavinden seg ned fra himmelen og rekker gutten en sammenbrettet, hvit duk.

english.anchor: “I haven’t got any meal,” said the North Wind.
english.caption: “But since you’re so badly off, you shall have a cloth.”
english.alt: Far in the north, where all the trees lean, the North Wind bends down out of the sky and hands the boy a folded white cloth.

illustrations.prompt: Evening in the Inn Parlour. On the small corner table, the white cloth with the red border is laid with a glistening joint of roast pork, a big platter of fish, new bread and, in the middle, a big bowl of cream porridge with a pool of melted butter in it as big as a pond. The Boy sits before it with a spoon, beaming. Beside him the landlady, a small, skinny woman with a sharp nose and a yellow kerchief, clasps her hands, her eyes shining greedily. At a long table, three travellers gape.

simplified.anchor: Han hadde knapt fått sagt det før duken gjorde det.
simplified.caption: En bolle rømmegrøt med et smørøye så stort som et tjern.
simplified.alt: På et bord i kroken på kroa står skinke, fisk, nystekt brød og en stor bolle rømmegrøt. Gutten smiler, og ved siden av står gjestgiverkona og ser grådig på duken.

english.anchor: And the cloth did just that.
english.caption: A bowl of cream porridge with a pool of butter as big as a millpond.
english.alt: On a corner table at the inn there is roast pork, fish, new bread and a big bowl of cream porridge. The boy beams, and beside him the innkeeper's wife stares greedily at the cloth.

illustrations.prompt: Inside the small, dim cottage by the cold blue light of a frosty window, the white cloth with the red border lies spread over the bare wooden table, completely empty. The Boy stands over it with his fists clenched and his jaw set, staring at it. Across the table the Mother sits on the bench with her arms folded and one eyebrow raised, giving him a long, dry look. A small fire smoulders in the hearth.

simplified.anchor: «Ja, nå har jeg sett det», sa moren.
simplified.caption: Duken dekket ikke opp med så mye som en bit flatbrød.
simplified.alt: Hjemme ligger duken tom på bordet. Gutten stirrer på den og biter tennene sammen, og moren sitter med armene i kors og ser tvilende på ham.

english.caption: The cloth didn’t serve up so much as a crust of flatbread.
english.alt: At home the cloth lies empty on the table. The boy stares at it with his jaw set, and his mother sits with her arms folded, looking at him doubtfully.

illustrations.prompt: In the Inn Parlour by firelight, gold ducats come ringing and tumbling onto the floorboards and lie in a shining heap under the Billy Goat's beard, a few still rolling away. The Boy stands beside the goat, delighted. In the doorway behind them, the Innkeeper watches with a much too wide smile, rubbing his hands together, his small eyes glittering as brightly as the gold.

simplified.anchor: Gjestgiveren sto og så på, og han syntes det var en flott bukk.
simplified.caption: Gjestgiveren syntes det var en flott bukk.
simplified.alt: Gullpenger triller ut på gulvet på kroa og blir liggende i en blank haug under skjegget til bukken. Gutten er glad, og i døra står gjestgiveren og gnir seg i hendene.

english.anchor: Out came the gold ducats, ringing and tumbling onto the floor
english.caption: The innkeeper thought that was a very fine goat indeed.
english.alt: Gold ducats tumble onto the floor of the inn and lie in a shining heap under the goat's beard. The boy is delighted, and in the doorway the innkeeper rubs his hands.

illustrations.prompt: Night in the Inn Parlour, lit only by the red glow of the embers. The Boy lies on a bench, snoring loudly with his mouth open, the old birch stick leaning against the wall beside him. The Innkeeper creeps up in his stocking feet with an identical stick in one hand and bends over the bench, stretching out the other hand for the real one. Unseen by him, one of the Boy's eyes has just opened.

simplified.anchor: Gjestgiveren skjønte også at kjeppen måtte være god for noe.
simplified.caption: Gutten lå på benken og snorket og lot som han sov.
simplified.alt: Om natta ligger gutten på en benk og later som han sover. Gjestgiveren lister seg bort med en kjepp som ligner, og strekker seg etter guttens kjepp.

english.anchor: The innkeeper had worked out that the stick must be good for something too.
english.caption: The boy lay on the bench, snoring and pretending to be asleep.
english.alt: At night the boy lies on a bench pretending to sleep. The innkeeper creeps over with a lookalike stick and reaches for the boy's stick.
